answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent auditors prove the account fabricated work or colluded. A single operator can still create many identities, but each one ties up more capital and risks a measurable loss; splitting a stake does not multiply its value. This makes Sybil influence costly rather than impossible: an echo of fake accounts must put real copper at risk, while honest participation can earn a pearl of reputation over time.
